item.title: Interview: The Bug That Charged Customers Twice
item.summary: In a job interview for a backend developer role, a candidate explains a difficult bug, how she found it and what she learned.
item.transcript_text:
Daniel: Thanks for coming in, Kamila. I'd like to start with something practical. Can you tell me about a bug that you found really difficult to fix?
Kamila: Sure, so last year I worked on the payment service for an online shop. Every few days, a small number of customers were charged twice for the same order.
Daniel: That sounds stressful. How did you approach it?
Kamila: Well, at first we couldn't reproduce it at all. Everything worked perfectly on our test servers. So I added more detailed logging and waited for it to happen again.
Daniel: And what did the logs show?
Kamila: They showed that when the network was slow, the mobile app sent the payment request a second time. Our server treated the two requests as two separate orders.
Daniel: Right, so it was a retry problem. How did you fix it?
Kamila: We gave every payment request a unique key. If the server receives the same key twice, it simply returns the first result instead of charging the customer again.
Daniel: Good, and looking back, what would you do differently?
Kamila: Honestly, I'd test for slow and unreliable networks from the start. We'd only tested the happy path, where everything goes right. I also learned to tell the support team about a problem early, so they can reassure customers while we're working on it.
Daniel: That's a really useful lesson. Okay, let's move on to some questions about databases.

options: It was too slow for mobile users.
Some customers paid twice for one order.
Customers could not log in to the shop.
Orders were sent to the wrong address.
questions.explanation: Kamila says: "a small number of customers were charged twice for the same order."

questions.prompt: Why was the bug hard to fix at first?
options: The logs had been deleted.
The mobile app was not finished.
The team could not make it happen on their test servers.
Customers did not report it.
questions.explanation: "At first we couldn't reproduce it at all. Everything worked perfectly on our test servers."

options: A mistake in the shop's prices
The server crashing at night
Customers clicking the button twice
The app sending the request again on a slow network

options: Repeated requests with the same key return the first result.
The app stopped working on slow networks.
Customers had to confirm every payment by phone.
The server deleted every second order.
questions.explanation: "If the server receives the same key twice, it simply returns the first result instead of charging the customer again."

questions.prompt: What does Kamila's last answer suggest about her?
options: She blames the support team for the problem.
She learns from mistakes and thinks about the customers.
She prefers to work alone.
She thinks testing is a waste of time.
questions.explanation: She would test unreliable networks "from the start" and tell support early "so they can reassure customers".
